clue.text: Expert's light touch with cards

definitions.note: read as 'Expert is', the 's joining the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: a dab is a light pat or touch
a hand is the set of cards a player holds

explanation.surface: A card sharp's skill lies in a deft, delicate touch when handling the deck.
explanation.definitionFit: A dab hand is a colloquial term for someone highly skilled at something, an expert.

clue.text: Information from page in browser

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a doe is a deer, and deer browse on leaves

explanation.surface: Someone gets data from a web page open in their internet browser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'browser' looks like web software but is a grazing deer, DOE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for inside information or the facts on something.

clue.text: Way in front, athlete 23

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 23 across, an officer of the police

parts.note: the bow is the front of a ship
a street is a road or way
a runner is a track athlete

explanation.surface: A sprinter far ahead of the field is described.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bow Street Runners were London's first professional police force, founded in the 18th century.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bow Street Runners were early London police officers, forerunners of the modern force.

clue.text: Twosome avoiding initial exposure

indicators.note: avoiding the initial means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a pairing is a couple or twosome

explanation.surface: A couple who shun being seen in public at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding initial' drops the P from PAIRING.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving an issue an airing exposes it to public view and discussion.

clue.text: Neglect of French entertainer heartless

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter is removed

parts.note: a diseuse is a woman who performs monologues, a term borrowed from French

explanation.surface: A cold, unfeeling French performer let things go to ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle E from DISEUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Disuse is the state of no longer being used, a form of neglect.

clue.text: Hilarious person inhales small quantity in fashionable club

indicators.note: something that inhales takes material inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a hoot is a very funny person
tsp, a teaspoon, is a small measured quantity

explanation.surface: A comedian at a trendy nightclub sneaks a little something up their nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small quantity' looks vague but is the recipe abbreviation for a teaspoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot spot is a lively, popular nightspot, a trendy place to be seen.

clue.text: Man trained with choir for musical

indicators.note: trained means the letters are drilled into a new shape, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man rehearsed alongside a choir for a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' rearranges MAN and CHOIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmonic is an adjective describing things relating to music or harmony.

clue.text: Boy about to be put into cot made of wood

parts.note: Tim is a boy's name

indicators.note: being put into something places a piece inside it

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A little lad is just about to be laid in his cot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to be' reads as one phrase but splits: 'about' is the leaf and 'to be put into' the container signal, the insertion landing between the cot's last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbered describes a structure built of timber, so made of wood.

clue.text: Albanian pirates tortured refugee

indicators.note: tortured means twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pirates from Albania tormented someone fleeing their homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tortured' rearranges ALBANIAN PIRATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Many Arabs displaced from Palestine became refugees, so the phrase serves as an example of a refugee.

clue.text: Bad stuttering may show evidence of intelligent behaviour

indicators.note: bad suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A poor stammer might suggest a person is clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' rearranges STUTTERING.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Turing's test judges whether a machine's responses show human-like intelligence.

clue.text: Very modest debtor might

parts.note: a penny, abbreviated p, is a very modest sum
a debtor is one who owes, an ower

explanation.surface: Someone owing very little might be the clue's whole story, a humble borrower.
explanation.walkthrough: The debtor of the surface owes just a penny: P plus OWER. 'might' is a noun here, not the verb it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Might as a noun means strength or force, a synonym of power.

clue.text: In dons' room fitter installs minute security device

parts.note: SCR, the senior common room, is where university dons relax

indicators.note: a fitter who installs something puts it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: fitter in the sense of more able, abler

explanation.surface: A tradesman puts in a security gadget inside the dons' common room at a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fitter' looks like a tradesman but is the comparative of fit, ABLER; 'installs' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrambler is a device that garbles a signal so eavesdroppers cannot understand it, a security measure.

clue.text: What peripatetic philosopher does is obvious

definitions.meaning: a peripatetic thinker walks while teaching, so is on his feet as he reasons
said of something plainly logical or self-evident

explanation.surface: A walking philosopher's habit is plain for all to see.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means something is logically evident; read literally, it describes a thinker upright while arguing.

clue.text: Before month half over, Democrat killed racist?

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before

indicators.note: half over means only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: June is a month
iced is slang for killed

explanation.surface: A political assassination, with a Democrat murdered before mid-month, prompts a question of bigotry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half over' keeps JU from JUNE (July works too). The question mark marks racist as one example of a prejudiced person.
explanation.definitionFit: A racist holds biased views against people of other races, one kind of bigoted person.

clue.text: Deplored coarse speaking

indicators.note: speaking signals that the word is to be taken by how it is said

parts.note: coarse behaviour or language is rude

explanation.surface: Someone condemned vulgar language.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplore something is to regret or lament it, as rued means regretted.

clue.text: Secure almost the best bottles shown initially here?

definitions.text: Secure almost the best bottles shown initially here?

parts.note: to secure a prize is to win it

indicators.note: to bottle something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within another
almost means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: the elite are the best of a group

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word shown

explanation.surface: A restaurant menu where you can get nearly the finest bottles on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ELITE to ELIT, which 'bottles' the S from 'shown initially'. The whole clue also describes where a diner sees the best bottles listed.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant's wine list is the menu showing which bottles are available.

clue.text: Wildly impetuous, missing note (you shouldn't have!) in soprano role

indicators.note: missing means the letter named is left out

parts.note: wildly impetuous behaviour is violent
N is a note, short for note in some music notation
said on receiving a gift, a polite thanks, ta

explanation.surface: A reckless singer playing a soprano part forgets a note and is thanked anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops N from VIOLENT. TA is a British colloquial thank-you.
explanation.definitionFit: Violetta is the soprano heroine of Verdi's La Traviata.

clue.text: Powerful Catholic overwhelmed by weakness

indicators.note: being overwhelmed by something means being engulfed, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a foible is a minor weakness
RC is the abbreviation for Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: A strong believer is overcome by a failing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overwhelmed by' is the container signal: the Catholic sits within the weakness.
explanation.definitionFit: Forcible means done with force, strong or powerful.

clue.text: Abandon working at landing places, lacking energy

indicators.note: lacking means the item named is removed from the word

parts.note: jetties are piers where boats land
E is the physics symbol for energy
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: An order to give up work at the docks for want of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes E from JETTIES to give JETTIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw overboard or discard, to abandon something.

clue.text: Pope is up for review

indicators.note: something up for review is to be gone over and reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The pontiff's position is being reconsidered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for review' rearranges IS UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Pius is the papal name taken by twelve popes, so it names a pope.

clue.text: Only fellow not given a grave

parts.note: sole means only

indicators.note: not given means the letter named is withheld from the word

parts.note: a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: The only man who was refused a burial plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like a noun for a burial place but is the adjective, serious.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave as an adjective means serious and sombre, a synonym.

clue.text: Expand very large element

parts.note: very large is OS, outsize, which is also the chemical symbol of an element; expanding that symbol gives its full name

explanation.surface: An instruction to enlarge a huge component.
explanation.walkthrough: OS for outsize is a clothing size; read as a chemical symbol Os, it expands to the element's full name.
explanation.definitionFit: The symbol Os in the periodic table stands for this dense metallic element.

clue.text: Cheating a pair of zebras?

definitions.meaning: betraying someone by deceit, a swindling act
zebra crossings are striped pedestrian crossings in Britain, so two of them make a twofold set of crossings

explanation.surface: A puzzled query whether two zebras could be fraudsters.
explanation.walkthrough: A zebra is the British name for a black-and-white striped pedestrian crossing on a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Double-crossing is betraying someone you pretend to help; literally it is two crossings.

clue.text: In poem, "maid" is "girl"

indicators.note: in means the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A literary note that a poem's word for a maid simply means a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' points to the letters inside POEM MAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is a girl's name, also the heroine of Jane Austen's novel.

clue.text: Artist, an apprehensive type?

definitions.meaning: John ... was an English landscape painter
a police officer apprehends, that is arrests, people, so is playfully apprehensive

explanation.surface: A painter who is a nervous sort of person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apprehensive' usually means anxious; here it means given to apprehending, arresting.
explanation.definitionFit: John Constable painted The Hay Wain; a police officer arrests, or apprehends, offenders.

clue.text: One is admitting personnel in pilgrim garb

indicators.note: admitting lets something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: one is the same as I am, said by oneself
HR, human resources, is the personnel department

explanation.surface: Someone lets staff in while wearing a pilgrim's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One is' must be read as a speaker saying of themselves 'I am'; 'admitting' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The ihram is the white seamless garment worn by Muslim pilgrims on the Hajj.

clue.text: Risk loading silver on back of truck? There's no written record of it

definitions.text: There's no written record of it

indicators.note: loading puts cargo inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: to risk something is to dare it

indicators.note: in an across clue, silver on the truck's last letter places it after
the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A haulier risks loading silver bullion onto the back of a lorry with no paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back of' takes the truck's final letter and 'on' puts silver after it, the across convention; 'loading' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark age is a period of history with little surviving documentation, so nothing written down about it.

clue.text: By main road, refuse collector about to leave north country

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest numbered main road, its 1 read as I

indicators.note: to leave means the letter named is taken out of the word

parts.note: a binman collects household rubbish

explanation.surface: A dustman by a highway is about to head away from the north toward a foreign country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' removes an N from BINMAN; 'about' reverses AI plus BIMAN. The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: Namibia is a country in south-western Africa.
